title: David's harp (1 Samuel 16:14–23)
hook: David plays and Saul's dark mood lifts

segments.voice: Yesterday, David, the youngest son, called in from the sheep and anointed in Bethlehem. Your line was the heart, not the height. What did you find in someone that you couldn't see at first? Today, the same chapter, in the palace. Day seven hundred thirty-five.

One verse says the spirit of the LORD came on David. The very next verse says it left Saul. And something else comes instead. The text calls it an evil spirit from the LORD, and it terrifies him. The king is in the dark, and his servants can see it. So they make a suggestion, the kind people still make for someone who's low. Let our lord command us, they say, to look for a man who can play the harp. When the dark comes on you, he'll play with his hand, and you'll be well. Saul says yes. Find me someone who plays well, and bring him to me.
screen: `THE SPIRIT LEAVES SAUL.` → `THE KING IS IN THE DARK.` → `FIND SOMEONE WHO CAN PLAY.`

segments.voice: One of the young men already knows someone. I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, he says: skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent, good-looking, and the LORD is with him. So Saul sends to Jesse: send me David your son, who is with the sheep. And Jesse loads a donkey with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat, and sends his youngest son to the king. Pause on what's happening. Nothing in the text says Saul knows what happened in Bethlehem, where this boy was just anointed with oil among his brothers. And David walks into the palace not as a rival, but as a musician, to help the man whose throne he'll one day sit on. Then the text says something tender: Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer. And Saul sends word to Jesse: let David stay with me, for he has found favor in my sight. Then the chapter ends with a picture. Whenever the spirit from God was upon Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand, and Saul found relief, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him. The Hebrew word for this harp is kinnor, a stringed instrument. The book doesn't tell us what he played, or whether there were words. Just that someone played, at the moment the dark came, and the king was well. This week we heard a boy say speak, a mother name what was lost, a people ask for a king, a king hide among the baggage, a king keep the showy offering, and a shepherd chosen for his heart. Today that shepherd sits down beside the king, and plays.
screen: `A SON OF JESSE WHO CAN PLAY.` · `THE RIVAL WALKS IN AS A HELPER.` · `SAUL LOVED HIM GREATLY.` · `THE DARK SPIRIT DEPARTED.` · then, large: `DAVID TOOK THE HARP, AND PLAYED WITH HIS HAND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: play music for someone who's low. Settle, and breathe. Think of one person who's in a dark stretch right now. Then think of one piece of music that might reach them. A song they love. A song from a better year. Something quiet. You don't need to play an instrument. You can send it, play it in the car with them, hum it on the phone, sit with them while it plays. For now, just choose the song, and hear a little of it in your head. If you pray, you can hold that person before God while you listen. The bell holds the time.
David's harp. The kinnor the young shepherd played for Saul, so that when the dark came, the king was refreshed and well. Today's word, and the close of a week in Samuel.
Your line: music lifts. Today, send the song you chose to the person you thought of, with no speech attached. Day seven hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Jews read David's playing for Saul as part of the Former Prophets; by tradition, David is also linked with the book of Psalms.

fork.setup: you're one of Saul's servants. the king is tormented and terrified, and nothing seems to help. what do you suggest?
options: call the priests to offer a sacrifice.
find a man who plays the harp well, to play when the dark comes.
leave the king alone until it passes.
fork.reveal: they suggest a harp player, and one of them already knows a son of Jesse. when David played, Saul was refreshed, and was well.

original.note: Hebrew: kinnor, the stringed instrument David played for Saul.

trapdoor: what you thought: a boy who played nice music.
what it means: the shepherd just anointed in Bethlehem walks into the palace as the king's helper, and his music lifts the king's darkness.
what a scholar hears: the spirit comes on David in one verse and leaves Saul in the next; the harp scene is built right on that turn.
